issues.original: If you know growth is coming, starting with custom often saves time and money in the long run.
issues.replacement: If you know growth is coming, it is worth weighing the cost of custom work against the time and money a later rebuild would take.
issues.reason: Removes an unsupported blanket claim that custom always saves time and money.

assessment.intent: Help a busy local business owner decide when a template is enough and when a tailored website is the better investment.
assessment.specificity: Good: decision worksheet, concrete service-page architecture, and local Okanagan framing keep the advice grounded.
assessment.evidence: Thin. The article mostly gives reasoned guidance. No client projects are cited, which fits, but the two unsupported claims need the fixes above.
assessment.voice: Clear, conversational and practical, in Michael's recommendation-driven register. Minimal padding and no smug contrast.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes, after the two narrow edits. The worksheet and page-architecture sample give owners something actionable rather than a generic template-versus-custom debate.
